newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks mark time in volume trade.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks mark time in volume trade.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed barely moved on Friday, but trading volume was marked by companies dressing up balance sheets, brokers said.
The all share index closed 0.31 points lower at 591.49. Walkers Tours fell 5.25 rupees to 13.25, Nestle one to 9.25.
"The index will be be ranged with many investors on holiday. But volumes could be high as companies dress up balance sheets," said K. Anurthan a trader at CDIC Sasoon Cumberbatch.
Turnover was 62.7 million rupees on 1.9 million shares. The main trades were 150,200 Distilleries at 6.75 rupees, 731,900 Kegalle Plantations at 23 and 654,000 Tea Services at 60.
Today's parcel of Kegalle Plantations and Thursday's quantity of 950,000 Kotgala Plantations at 26, were underwriters selling devolvements at huge profits, brokers said.
The initial public offers of the two companies were underwritten by the state-owned Bank of Ceylon, National Development Bank and Merchant Bank of Sri Lanka, at 10 rupees.
"Though everyone expects a low level of activity, don't be surprised if you see some big buyers using the lethargy to pick bargains," said Nanda Nair research director of brokerage John Keells.
